Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand the main integration points and the spike patterns you see during morning syncs. As promised, recap + next steps so we can kick off the POC smoothly.

Recap / Proposed POC scope (high level)
- Goal: Validate latency and cost for your primary clinical-insights flow (patient summary + extraction) under realistic traffic.
- Success criteria: 95th pct latency <= 350ms for single-request interactive flows; throughput to support steady-state and peak-day spikes with graceful degradation.
- Duration: 3-week trial (config + 2-week run + evaluation).

Requests / next steps for AcmeHealth (can you confirm the items below?)
1) Workload profile (we attached a small spreadsheet): steady RPS, peak RPS, concurrency, typical prompt/response token lengths, burst duration/patterns.
2) Success criteria & evaluation: confirm any KPIs you want us to measure (latency pcts, error rates, cost per 1k tokens, quality regression targets).
3) Timeline & kickoff: propose kickoff next Tue 3/16 for a quick alignment + handoff to Marissa (CS) and Dylan (technical lead).
4) Security/compliance contacts: include who will own the SOC2 evidence requests or security questionnaire.

Attached: workload_profile.xlsx — please fill the sheet with the numbers you can share. If anything is sensitive, upload to your secure drive and we can pull from there.

I'll follow up with a proposed mutual action plan once we have the workload numbers.

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching a short requirements doc and I filled the intake spreadsheet with our best estimates so you can size things. Key numbers below (preliminary):

- Typical steady RPS: 8 RPS (internal UI traffic outside business hours)
- Morning peak: sustained ~120 RPS for 20-30 minutes (internal batch sync + clinician bulk queries)
- Highest burst observed: 250 RPS for ~10 minutes (rare, occurs during daily sync + outage retries)
- Concurrency: up to 30 concurrent interactive sessions (mostly clinicians)
- Prompt length (user input): median ~120 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens
- Response length (model reply): median ~300 tokens, 95th ~900 tokens
- Average tokens per request (prompt+response): ~420 tokens
- Typical latency expectation: interactive flows should feel sub-second; target to evaluate <= 350-400ms P95 for the main endpoint

Success criteria we care about:
- <1% error rate for the trial window
- P95 latency within agreed threshold for interactive flows (above)
- No data leakage and logs retained per our policy (we will share retention requirements in the security questionnaire)
- Cost per 1k tokens estimate to compare against our internal budget

Security contact: Sanjay Patel (sanjay.patel@acmehealth.com) — he will be the owner for evidence and questionnaire.

Attached: acme_poc_requirements.pdf (high-level requirements) and I updated workload_profile.xlsx.

On timeline, 3-week trial sounds good. We can do kickoff on Tue 3/16 at 10am PT.

—Laura

Laura / Sanjay — great, thanks for the quick turnaround and the filled intake. A few clarifications and a proposed plan:

Clarifications (from the numbers you provided)
- When you say "morning peak ~120 RPS", is that spread across multiple endpoints or concentrated on the single clinical-insights API we discussed? If multiple, can you split by endpoint in the sheet?
- For bursts (250 RPS for ~10m), is that typically back-to-back (several bursts over the hour) or a single spike?

Proposed Redwood plan for POC
- Week 0 (3/16): Kickoff + RG meeting — confirm SLOs, get signed intake and security contact access.
- Week 1: Provision trial environment (private sandbox) with conservative instance sizing. Run synthetic load that mirrors steady + morning peak.
- Week 2: Run customer-driven tests (your QA team runs representative workload) + iterate config (batching, KV cache, quantization profile).
- Week 3: Final run + evaluation, generate report (latency pcts, cost projection, edge-case logs).

Initial sizing ask from our infra team (tentative) — we'll finalize after endpoint split:
- Baseline: 4 x A10G-equivalent GPUs (quantized model) for steady-state + 1 autoscale group for peak bursts.
- If bursts are frequent and sustained, we will recommend adding 2 GPUs or switching to higher-memory instances to keep P95 low.

Action items / owners
- AcmeHealth: fill endpoint split in sheet (Laura / Sanjay) — due EOD Thu 3/18.
- Redwood CS: Marissa Cole will run kickoff and own POC coordination.
- Redwood Solutions: Dylan Brooks will pick instance types and run initial capacity tests.
- Redwood Sales: Ben Carter will manage terms + mutual action plan.

Attached: POC_scope_v1.pdf (draft mutual action plan). Can we confirm Tue 3/16 10am PT for kickoff? I can set the invite once you confirm.
